headline: Ben and Orest cash in on collision wins to lead early
dek: Week 1 brought us two NFC West collisions — and both home teams left licking their wounds. Ben's Niners and Orest's Seahawks grabbed the early advantage while five entrants sat idle watching their teams on bye.
takeaways: Both collisions went to the road teams — Ben's 49ers boat-raced Tymko's Rams, Orest's Seahawks edged Adrian's Patriots in a gritty defensive affair.
Drew Lock outdueled Drake Maye in a preseason quarterback battle nobody asked for but we all had to watch anyway.
Ben's +20 net on the week is the largest margin we'll see until someone's team remembers how to play offense.

games.text:
Orest's Seahawks survived a rock fight in Seattle, holding off Adrian's Patriots 13-10 in a game that made punters feel relevant again. Drew Lock managed the game competently enough — 16/22 for 187 yards and a touchdown — while Jaxon Smith-Njigba did the heavy lifting with 8 catches for 122 yards and the game's lone receiving score. The Patriots' Drake Maye had a forgettable debut, tossing three interceptions against just one touchdown on 23/33 passing. Rhamondre Stevenson ground out 51 yards on 18 carries, but New England's offense sputtered whenever it sniffed the red zone.

This was the week's tightest collision, and Orest walks away with the full point while Adrian takes the early collar. The margin was just three points, but those three picks from Maye were the difference — you can't gift a competent defense that many opportunities and expect to steal one on the road. Adrian's Patriots showed some fight, but moral victories don't move you up the standings when you're already sitting in eighth place after one week.

Ben's 49ers made an emphatic statement in Los Angeles, dismantling Tymko's Rams 27-7 in a game that was never competitive after the first quarter. Brock Purdy was efficient and deadly, going 25/34 for 205 yards and three touchdowns, spreading the wealth across his receiving corps. Christian McCaffrey added 68 yards on the ground on just 10 carries, reminding everyone why he's the most dangerous dual-threat back in football. The Rams' offense, meanwhile, looked completely lost — Matthew Stafford managed just 155 yards on 15/25 passing with an interception, and despite Blake Corum's 54 rushing yards, the entire unit looked out of sync.

This collision wasn't close, and Ben's 20-point net advantage has him sitting alone atop the standings after Week 1. Tymko, on the other hand, takes the worst loss of the week and finds himself in the cellar at 0-1 with a -20 net. The Rams showed nothing resembling a functional offense, and if that continues, Tymko's going to need his Chiefs to carry serious water all season long. Ben, meanwhile, can sit back and wait for his Texans to take the field, already banking a point and feeling pretty good about life.

entrants.name: Ben
entrants.text: Leads the pool after one week with his Niners' dominant road win over the Rams. His Texans are still on bye but he's already got breathing room with a +20 net. Next week brings a collision with Chris — Bills at Texans — where Ben can extend his lead or watch it evaporate in a hurry.

entrants.name: Orest
entrants.text: Sits second on the tiebreaker after his Seahawks gutted out the ugly win over the Patriots. The three-point margin isn't impressive, but a collision win is a collision win. His Ravens hit the road to Indy next week, where he'll try to get to 2-0 before most of the pool wakes up.

entrants.name: Bill, Chris, Jordy, Matej, Taras
entrants.text: All watched Week 1 from the sidelines with both teams on bye. The good news: nobody lost ground. The bad news: Ben and Orest are already a game ahead. Chris faces a collision in Houston next week, while the others finally get on the board.

entrants.name: Adrian
entrants.text: Drake Maye's three-pick debut cost him the collision with Orest, and now he's chasing from eighth place. His Bucs travel to Cincinnati next week — he needs that one badly or he's staring at an 0-2 hole before September ends.

entrants.name: Tymko
entrants.text: The Rams laid an absolute egg at home, gifting Ben 20 net points and leaving Tymko in last place after one week. His Chiefs host Jordy's Broncos on Monday night in another collision — lose that and he's 0-2 in collisions before Week 2 even starts. Not ideal.

ahead: Week 2 brings two more collisions: Chris's Bills at Ben's Texans on Sunday afternoon, and Jordy's Broncos at Tymko's Chiefs on Monday night.
Tymko desperately needs his Chiefs to show up — another collision loss would put him in a crater he might not climb out of.
Five entrants who sat out Week 1 finally get both teams in action, so the standings are about to get a lot more interesting.
